title: Slap-tonguing, instrument prices and Stradivarius violins
summary: Holmes used to slap-tongue, remembers cheap altos, clarinets and sopranos at about a hundred dollars, and scoffs at thousand-dollar horns and expensive violins.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Well, they (?) with cigarette lighters and heat them and...
Yeah, yeah. Well, they do everything. You know what I mean? Burn them on the edge. Put them on a quarter and burn the edge, the tip of it, all that kind of stuff.
Well, did you ever try any slap-tonguing or any of that?
I used to slap-tongue years ago.
Yeah?
Holmes (1/14) - 28

Sure. Everybody did. Yeah, that was just going along with the times. If you had to do certain things, you did it. If you had to play clarinet, you had to play clarinet. And soprano saxophone, too. Practically everybody had an alto, a clarinet and a soprano. Everybody had them... Those that could afford them. Those instruments weren't sky-high like they are today. You could get an alto for around a hundred dollars. A good-name alto cost you a few more dollars. You could get a good alto for a hundred dollars. And a clarinet, you could get them dirt-cheap. And sopranos didn't cost too much either. They were cheaper than the altos.
But nowadays, I don't know. I haven't priced any instruments lately, but they tell they're around up there in the thousand-dollar class.
Yeah, they are.
Boy..> That's second-hand.
Well, some of them, yes.

A thousand dollars second-hand. I see it in the book, in the Union Book. You know, they have the instruments for sale, used, this-that-and-the-other, and they've got the prices that they want for them. And then flutes, they're out of reach. I think I saw a flute in there for thirty thousand dollars second-hand. Thirty
Holmes (1/14) - 29
thousand dollars for a flute. What can a flute do for thirty thousand dollars?
Well, they've got violins that are...
Now, there's something... Now, what can a violin do for that much money... One of them Stradivariuses. What can it do for that much money? You drop it and you have nothin'!
But apparently, the violinist perceives a difference in tone and...
It still sounds like a violin to me. Some violins sound good. No, all violins sound bad; some sound worse. No, some violins are... I mean, the Stradivarius... You can tell quality, though.
Yeah.
Yeah, some violins ..(?)..
